name: StellarFS
problem: Standard user-space file systems rely on heavy kernel modules or lack robust copy-on-write structural sharing, transparent block deduplication, and crash-safe transactional journaling.
pain: Developers experimenting with custom file system architectures must interface with complex OS-specific FUSE bindings or write unsafe disk-allocation logic from scratch.
solution: A zero-dependency, user-space virtual file system and storage container written in C11. It implements a custom block allocator, an on-disk B+Tree inode index, cryptographic block-level deduplication using SHA-256 digests, transparent LZ4-style block compression, a multi-version crash-safe journaling log, sparse file mapping, hierarchical directory trees, and an exhaustive fault-injection test runner.
verification: Deterministic integration suite injecting bit-flip corruptions, power failures mid-journal-write, and out-of-space allocations to verify recovery invariants.
major_features: Custom block allocator managing fixed-size storage partitions with bitmap free-space tracking
On-disk B+Tree inode index mapping file paths to block pointer arrays
Cryptographic block deduplication engine using SHA-256 content hashing to eliminate redundant blocks
Transparent block compression subsystem compressing individual disk pages before allocation
Write-ahead journaling log providing crash-safe atomicity for multi-block directory updates
Sparse file allocation engine handling unallocated holes without consuming physical disk sectors
Hierarchical directory lookup parser supporting nested path traversal and hard link resolution
Fault-injection test suite simulating power cuts, truncated files, and damaged block bitmaps
truth_policy: Only validated behavior may be claimed as working.
